item.title: Urakami Cathedral — Guide
item.description: Urakami Cathedral, in the north of Nagasaki, is a red-brick Catholic church with a poignant history bound up with both the persecution of Christians and the atomic bomb. Built by local Catholics in the early twentieth century — descendants of the ‘hidden Christians’ who had secretly kept their faith through 250 years of brutal persecution — it was once the largest church in East Asia. On 9 August 1945 it stood just 500 metres from the hypocentre and was almost completely destroyed, killing those inside.
